field.label: Key Theory / Methodology
field.value: Cancer arises from cells harbouring many mutations that distinguish them from normal cells. A subset of those will be driver mutations that contribute to tumorigenesis and disease progression. My research is built on the principle that important driver mutations will arise in many different cancer patients due to positive selection, and seeks to functionally validate candidate driver mutations using molecular and cell biology techniques.

bilingual.english: Cancer arises from cells harbouring many mutations that distinguish them from normal cells. A subset of those will be driver mutations that contribute to tumorigenesis and disease progression. My research is built on the principle that important driver mutations will arise in many different cancer patients due to positive selection, and seeks to functionally validate candidate driver mutations using molecular and cell biology techniques.

field.label: Research Interests
field.value: I am interested in the genetic basis of disease and in the cell and molecular biological processes that are disrupted in disease. My PhD research utilized a model organism to dissect the mechanisms of ciliary length control, and my motivation was to understand how known human disease mutations could alter ciliary length. My postdoctoral research is aimed at identifying mutations that drive cancer formation and progression. I am interested in the molecular biological processes that cause mutations in cancer, and in characterizing the wild-type and mutant versions of genes affected by driver mutations.

field.label: Research Experience Summary
field.value: My PhD work used the single-celled alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii as a model system to study the mechanisms of ciliary assembly and disassembly. More recently, we used mutagenesis and whole genome sequencing to identify novel genes involved in a particular type of ciliary disassembly known as deflagellation. I have since transitioned to using genomics tools to identify driver mutations in non-Hodgkin lymphomas, while relying on my cell and molecular biology background to determine the functions of genes affected by driver mutations.

field.value: Molecular and cell biology of cancer

field.label: Course Description
field.value:
In 2012, cancer was the number one cause of death in Canada, responsible for 30% of all deaths. During this course we will examine the fundamental cell and molecular biology, genetics, and physiology of cancer, with the goal of understanding why this disease is so deadly, and why we continue to lose the battle against it. In addition, we will explore the history of cancer research and treatment to understand how cancer has helped shape modern biomedical research.
The primary emphasis of this course will be on critical reading of primary scientific literature. Nearly every class will include student-led discussions of research papers. It will be fast-paced and challenging.
